The height y metres of a javelin at horizontal distance x metres is modelled by y = ax² + bx + c. It passes through (1, 13.95), (4, 18) and (5, 18.55). (a) Write down a system of three equations in a, b and c. (b) Solve it to find a, b and c. (c) Find the maximum height and the horizontal distance at which y = 0.
items.markingKey: (a) 1a + 1b + c = 13.95, … (A1 A1). (b) GDC (M1): a = −0.2, b = 2.35, c = 11.8 (A1). (c) vertex x = −b/(2a) = 5.88 (M1), max height 18.7 m (A1); y = 0 at x = 15.5 m (A1) (reject negative root, R1).

items.stem: (a) Solve the equation 3·4ˣ = 7^(x + 2), giving the exact answer in terms of natural logarithms and its value to 3 s.f. (b) Explain why taking logarithms is necessary here. (c) Verify your answer using a GDC graph or table.
items.answer: (a) x = (2 ln 7 − ln 3)/(ln 4 − ln 7) = −4.99 (b) unknown in the exponents with different bases
items.markingKey: (a) take ln of both sides (M1): ln 3 + x ln 4 = (x + 2) ln 7 (A1); collect x terms (M1); x = −4.99 (A1). (b) R1 the bases cannot be made equal. (c) A1 intersection of the two graphs at x = −4.99.

Outline the meaning of the term "natural logarithm".
items.answer: The logarithm with base e ≈ 2.718, written ln x = log_e x

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "root of a polynomial equation"?
options: The logarithm with base 10, written log x = log₁₀ x
Denoted x^(1/n): the number which, raised to the power n, gives x
A value of x that makes the polynomial equal to zero; graphically an x-intercept of y = p(x)
The statement that log_a b = c means a^c = b: the logarithm is the exponent to which the base must be raised
items.answer: A value of x that makes the polynomial equal to zero; graphically an x-intercept of y = p(x)
items.markingKey: C. "root of a polynomial equation" is a value of x that makes the polynomial equal to zero; graphically an x-intercept of y = p(x).

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "change of base"?
options: Given by log_a x = log_b x / log_b a, used to evaluate logs in any base with ln or log₁₀
The logarithm with base e ≈ 2.718, written ln x = log_e x
The logarithm with base 10, written log x = log₁₀ x
Two or more linear equations in the same unknowns that must be satisfied simultaneously
items.answer: Given by log_a x = log_b x / log_b a, used to evaluate logs in any base with ln or log₁₀
items.markingKey: A. "change of base" is given by log_a x = log_b x / log_b a, used to evaluate logs in any base with ln or log₁₀.

items.markingKey: R1 (b^m)^(1/n) = (b^(1/n))^m by the law (aᵖ)^q = a^(pq); R1 taking the root first (3) avoids large numbers like 27; A1 3.

The populations of two villages t years after 2020 are modelled by P_A = 450e^(0.196t) for Porto Novo and P_B = 2439e^(0.012t) for Cusco. (a) Find the population of each village in 2030. (b) Find the value of t when the populations are equal, using logarithms. (c) Comment on the validity of using these models for 50 years.
items.markingKey: (a) 3195 (A1), 2750 (A1). (b) 450e^(0.196t) = 2439e^(0.012t) ⇒ e^(0.184t) = 2439/450 (M1); t = ln(5.42)/0.184 (M1) = 9.19 (A1). (c) R1 exponential models predict unlimited growth; resources, migration and policy limit populations.
